Container.Name: Gamekeep
Container.Overview:
Let your friends restart your game servers without giving them access to Unraid.
They sign in, see which servers are up and how many people are playing, and press Restart when a game update lands. A cooldown stops anyone restarting a server that is still booting, and a shared activity log shows who did what.
Three roles: owner (everything), operator (install, stop, start and restart servers), member (restart only).
Also included: live CPU and memory graphs with 24h history, an environment-variable editor, a file browser with backups on every change, installing new game servers straight from Community Applications, and optional port forwarding through your router.
IMPORTANT - read before installing: This container mounts the Docker socket, which is root-equivalent on your server. It only ever touches the containers you list in its config file, and it never lets a request name a container directly. Even so, treat the owner password like your Unraid root password, and put Cloudflare Access or similar in front if you expose it to the internet.
FIRST RUN: Leave PUBLIC_URL as the address you will actually use. On first start the log prints a one-time SETUP TOKEN - open the WebUI, paste it, and create the owner account. Nobody can claim that account without reading your container log.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the portal. Not needed if you put a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel on the same Docker network.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: How the portal restarts your game servers. Required.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Accounts, audit log, metrics and cached artwork. Use a POOL path (/mnt/cache/...) and not /mnt/user - SQLite and the FUSE layer do not get along.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Holds servers.json, which lists the containers this portal may touch. Read-only on purpose: it IS the whitelist.

Config.Name: Game server data
Config.Description: Where servers deployed through the portal keep their files. Must match APPDATA_HOST_ROOT below.

Config.Name: Unraid templates
Config.Description: Optional. Lets servers deployed through the portal show up properly in your Docker tab instead of as orphan images.

Config.Name: PUBLIC_URL
Config.Description: The address people will type, e.g. https://portal.example.com or http://192.168.1.10:8088. Decides whether session cookies are marked Secure, so get it right once you are on HTTPS.

Config.Name: SESSION_SECRET
Config.Description: At least 32 characters. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32 - changing it signs everyone out.

Config.Name: APPDATA_HOST_ROOT
Config.Description: The SAME directory as the Game server data path above, but as the HOST sees it. Docker resolves bind mounts against the host, so a mismatch here silently writes game data to the wrong place.

Config.Name: APPDATA_ROOT
Config.Description: The same directory as the container sees it. Leave as-is unless you changed the mount above.

Config.Name: LAN_ADDRESS
Config.Description: Optional. Your Unraid server's address on the LAN, e.g. 192.168.1.10. Used to tell you which port forwards a new game server needs, and to create them if you connect a router.

Config.Name: TRUSTED_PROXIES
Config.Description: Which sources may set X-Forwarded-For. This decides what the audit log records as a visitor's IP address. The default trusts the Docker bridge range, where a reverse proxy or cloudflared lives. Widen deliberately or not at all.

Config.Name: TRUSTED_PUBLISHERS
Config.Description: Optional. Whose game servers may be installed from Community Applications, comma separated. Deploying a container is root-equivalent, so this is a trust list. Leave empty for the built-in default.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone, so the audit log reads in your local time.
